verses.text: "Build an altar of acacia wood. It is to be square, about two and a quarter metres long and two and a quarter metres wide, and about one and a third metres high.
Make a horn at each of its four corners, so that the horns and the altar are one piece. Cover the altar with bronze.
Make all its tools out of bronze: its pots for removing the ashes, and its shovels, bowls, meat forks, and fire pans.
Make a grate for it, a bronze net, and make a bronze ring at each of the four corners of the net.
Put the grate under the ledge of the altar, so that it reaches halfway up the altar.
Make poles of acacia wood for the altar and cover them with bronze.
Put the poles through the rings, so that they are on both sides of the altar when it is carried.
Make the altar hollow, out of boards. Make it just as you were shown on the mountain.
Make a courtyard for the holy tent. The south side is to be forty-five metres long, with curtains of fine twisted linen.
It is to have twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The north side is also to be forty-five metres long, with curtains, twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the posts.
The west end of the courtyard is to be twenty-two metres wide, with curtains, ten posts, and ten bases.
The east end, towards the sunrise, is also to be twenty-two metres wide.
On one side of the entrance there are to be curtains almost seven metres long, with three posts and three bases.
On the other side there are also to be curtains almost seven metres long, with three posts and three bases.

For the entrance to the courtyard, make a screen nine metres long of blue, purple, and red yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of someone who sews beautiful patterns. It is to have four posts and four bases.
All the posts around the courtyard are to have silver bands and hooks, and bronze bases.
The courtyard is to be forty-five metres long and twenty-two metres wide, with curtains of fine twisted linen over two metres high, and with bronze bases.
All the tools used in the service of the holy tent, and all its tent pegs and the pegs of the courtyard, are to be made of bronze.
Command the people of Israel to bring you pure oil from pressed olives for the lamps, so that the lamps can keep burning all the time.

In the Tent of Meeting, outside the curtain that hangs in front of the covenant box, Aaron and his sons are to keep the lamps burning in front of the LORD from evening until morning. This is a law for the people of Israel that will last forever, for all generations."
